title: THEY CALLED THEIR BRAND WHAT?! Nice frame tho...

takeaways.text: The frame is not a copied Aethos: the lowered seat tube leaves more exposed seatpost on small sizes, which he says helps comfort for short riders.
His mechanic built an XXS without the usual sanding or chasing, and the clear-coated carbon showed no flaws; the frame comes with several headset covers for different routing options.
Even in XXS, too small for him, it tracked and turned in well on a local descent, unlike most extra-small frames he has ridden.
His size-XS Team Edition frame, claimed to use Mitsubishi carbon equivalent to T1100, weighed 673 g with derailleur hanger and bottle-cage bolts and a T47 shell.

disclosure: China Cycling's presenter also runs Panda Podium, which sells BIGROCK frames. The video does not name the model, but shows the same XXS regular and XS Team Edition frames as his later Sohtea long-term review.
summary: A first look at BIGROCK's road frame, regular and Team Edition, built up at Panda Podium.
